Consigner or Cx or Customer: Users who have truck requirements
Demand_id: This is generated for each demand created by consigner by providing origin, destination and vehicle type. The total count of demands might not represent the actual shipment requirements for a consigner as the consigner might make multiple demands for same requirement due to multiple issues - price browsing, consignee cancelled order, etc. Generally, we calculate most of the metrics at demand level but in few cases, we also calculate metrics at ODVT/CODVT/COD level.
ODVT -  If we have to calculate a metric at ODVT level then it means replacing demand_id with combination of date,consigner_code, origin_id, destination_id and vt_id and then we can aggregate this id over any timeperiod or dimension.
CODVT - If we have to calculate a metric at CODVT level then it means replacing demand_id with combination of date,consigner_code, origin_cluster_id, destination_id and vt_id and then we can aggregate this id over any timeperiod or dimension. We generally consider count of CODVTs to be a good represntation of actual shipment requirements of the consigner but we dont apply this by default to the metrics unless asked to do so.
COD - If we have to calculate a metric at COD level then it means replacing demand_id with combination of date,consigner_code, origin_cluster_id and destination_id and then we can aggregate this id over any timeperiod or dimension.

The price at which we found the vehicle is known as Supply Fare (supply_fare in table). We deduct FO commission (fo_commission in table) from this amount and so we get the net payable to FO. We add a markup over Supply Fare (also known as middle share) and show it to the consigner. This price is known as Base Price (base_price in table). This price is might be anywhere in or outside the range shown to the consigner before we search for the vehcile ; range shown is from base_rate1 to base_rate3. We then add a service charge to the Base Price and get Consigner Freight Fare (consigner_freight_fare in table). We now deduct discounts (if appicable) to the Consigner Freight Fare to get the Final Price that is payable by the consigner to us.\

Trucking Logistics - Part Truck Load (PTL)

A PTL aggregator on the WheelsEye marketplace: the consigner enters a lane (pickup + drop pincode), weight and box size, and compares rates, TAT and on-time performance from 100+ PTL transporters in one place, then books, pays and tracks the shipment.
PTL is built on top of the FTL (MP) consigner base. It is wallet-share expansion for existing FTL consigners, not a new-logo business: ~35-40% of FTL consigners also have PTL needs.
PTL is NOT defined by weight. It is defined by the product flow (Part Load tab / web portal / ops entry). Never filter by weight to separate PTL from FTL. Weight is only a reporting band: 0-300 / 300-1000 / 1000+ kg.

Different product, unit economics, SLAs, supply and ops flow. Do not transfer FTL logic to PTL.
- FTL: a whole truck (vehicle type) is matched/bid by an FO; price = supply_fare + markup; demand key = ODVT.
- PTL: the consigner buys space by chargeable weight (₹/kg) from a transporter's network; price comes from transporter rate cards; demand key = requirement (see Key Terms).
- FTL is the core business. PTL must not cannibalise FTL (see FTL Guardrail).

4. BULK_UPLOAD: from 15 Oct 2026, price check + demand created together by an upload. Often back-entered after delivery: keep in volume counts, exclude from conversion rates.

Consigner / Cx: user with a shipment requirement (demand side). Never conflate with FO or transporter (supply side).
Transporter / TPT: PTL supply - a 3PL or local transporter that carries the shipment. Not an FO.
Price check: one rate-API call = one row in fact_ptl_browsing (browsing_id). Includes automatic re-quotes from the transporter screen, so rows are NOT user searches. ~3x more price checks than requirements.
Requirement: the PTL equivalent of a real shipment need (closest analogue to FTL CODVT). = one consigner x one lane (pickup + drop pincode), grouping price checks with < 30 min gap (datediff in seconds < 1800). It counts as a requirement only if: booked, OR channel is web portal / bulk upload / ODIN, OR (app) at least 1 change from the prefill (drop != 560001, weight != 200, or dimensions entered), OR the continue / transporter-select event or a later booking step fired. Count with sum(requirement_flag).
Demand (demand_id): created when the consigner selects a transporter and taps continue (new flow: Android 1770+, iOS 1080+, consigner web 2.4.0+; web portal from 16 Oct 2026 15:48 IST at 'Create Pickup Request'). Before the new flow, a demand existed only after 'Pay and book', so demand ~= placement.
Would-be demand: a demand the old flow would have created, backfilled from events. demand_id = 'B/<browsing_id>'. Included in demand_flag.
Placement / Booking: demand booked and paid (placement_flag).
Pickup: pickup_done_time not null (pickup_flag). In-transit comes ~12 h later.
PTL acquisition: first pickup_done_time per consigner. dim_consigners.acquisition_date_ptl is the DEMAND date of the first PTL trip, not the pickup date.
Trip (fact_ptl_requirements.trip_flag): trip_end OR in_transit OR pickup_done not null, AND not cancelled/expired.
Delivered: trip_end_time not null (delivered_flag).
PTL-live consigner: allocated SHOW_PTL (variant 17) with deleted = false.
Dual user: consigner with both FTL and PTL trips. Dual users share an origin ~84% of the time but the full lane only ~16% - map lanes from pincode, never by city strings.

Line of Business (FTL): PTL Supply (context, not Demand POD scope) (PTL)
Trucking Logistics:
Transporter types:
- 3PL (organized): Delhivery, DP World, Xpressbees (V-Trans is organized too). Best priced at 0-300 kg.
- Local transporters: everyone else; separate first-mile + last-mile and lower base freight. Best priced at 300-1000 / 1000+ kg.
No flag in data - classify by the name list.
Our mix today: 3PL ~80-90%, local ~10-20% (industry is roughly inverted). Expected to drift toward local as we scale.
Supply modes: Spot (tentative rate), Testing-contractual, Contractual (fixed rate). Contractual is ~0 today.
Serviceability: a transporter serves a lane if it covers the loading pincode (pickup_available = true) and the unloading pincode and has an active zonal rate for that zone pair. Supply comes from the rate engine tables, not Google sheets.
Transporter attribution = who ACTUALLY carried it (consignment operator), not selected_tpt.
SLA adherence on pickup, delivery and visibility is currently weak across both 3PL and local. 'SLAs improve once we route enough volume to a transporter' is a hypothesis to validate, not a fact.

Price is computed per transporter on the lane (backend PriceCheckService):
1. Chargeable weight (CW) = max(min chargeable weight, volumetric weight, actual weight). Volumetric = (L x W x H / volumetric factor) x qty x CFT from the transporter's rate metadata. Bulky-light cargo is priced on volume.
2. Base freight = max(base ₹/kg (zonal rate + to-pincode additional rate) x CW, min base freight).
3. Add: fuel surcharge (% of base freight), handling, docket (flat), FOV, labour, appointment, pickup / delivery ODA, first-mile and last-mile (by service type), special/odd-dimension charges.
4. Less discounts (e.g. first-booking discount, ADVANCE payment-plan discount).
5. GST 18% on top (0 when to-pay).
What the consigner sees: base ₹/kg (ex GST) as the headline per transporter, then the all-in total once weight and box size are entered.
Take rate (all-inclusive, matches the PnL dashboard) = (consigner fare - operator fare) / consigner fare, GST excluded, where fare = base freight + expenses. Attribute by actual operator; exclude internal test accounts WE180649, WE5273773, WE6413979.

Consigner pays at booking (Pay and book = placement); insufficient wallet balance shows a top-up / payment link. Many PTL consigners are used to to-pay (consignee pays the transporter on delivery) - a known adoption barrier. Payment-flow experiment: variants 36 PTL_DEFAULT_PAYMENT_FLOW / 37 PTL_DIVIDE_PAYMENT_FLOW.

Shipper-facing ETA = the transporter's ETA padded by that transporter's historical performance (eta_date); tpt_eta_date = raw transporter ETA.
Late = done on a later calendar day than the ETA (*_eta_diff > 0).
For the customer promise use the ORIGINAL delivery ETA and the REQUESTED pickup ETA (the latest ETA is re-baselined).
Check the denominator (placed vs picked up) before comparing SLA metrics.
Delay types: blank = on time, BREACH BY 1-2d, BREACH BY >2d, LOCATION_NOT_UPDATED, ETA_CHANGED.

Proof of delivery uploaded after trip end. pod_validity: OK / SUBJECT_TO_VERIFICATION / NOT_OKAY_DAMAGED / NOT_OKAY_SHORTAGE / WRONG_DOCUMENT / STAMP_AND_SIGN_MISSING. Damage fear is a stated PTL adoption barrier.
